message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (dir. Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** (dir. Stanley Kubrick) | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** (dir. John Carpenter) | A tense, claustrophobic survival horror with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** (dir. M. Night Shyamalan) | A twist‑filled thriller that blends supernatural elements with emotional depth. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (dir. Danny Boyle) | Fast‑paced, post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (dir. James Wan) | Dark, gritty, and full of inventive traps that keep you on edge. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (dir. James Wan) | A modern classic that balances jump scares with atmospheric dread. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (dir. Drew Goddard) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and genuinely scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (dir. David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that’s as clever as it is terrifying. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (dir. John Krasinski) | Tension built around silence, with a strong family dynamic. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** (dir. Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that’s unsettlingly beautiful and psychologically intense. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** (dir. Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling that mixes sci‑fi with psychological terror. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (dir. Gerard Johnstone) | A creepy, tech‑savvy horror that taps into our fears of AI. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want a psychological thriller, a supernatural scare, or something that pushes the boundaries of the genre!
